newsitem.title: UK: London gold eases amid bearish market mood.
newsitem.headline: London gold eases amid bearish market mood.

text.p: Gold prices drifted lower towards a key support level on Tuesday amid increasingly bearish market sentiment, dealers said.
But prices steadied after early losses and the market appeared undecided whether to test recent lows at $377 an ounce, a move analysts said may spark a tumble to fresh 19-month lows.
"It's drifting lower more on bearish sentiment than anything else," one London-based dealer said.
Bullion fixed at $378.20 an ounce, little changed from the morning fixing of $378.30. But it was down nearly $1.00 from Monday's afternoon fixing of $379.10.
Market sentiment turned bearish late last week after heavy selling by gold producers stalled a brisk rally at a peak of nearly $385 an ounce and turned prices lower.
One analyst noted that gold had failed to dip below $378 so far this week and prices may be bottoming out at current levels before tackling upside resistance levels.
But the chance of more selling pressure remained as price charts painted a vulnerable picture for gold, analysts said.
Over the past two months gold has twice bounced from 19-month lows just under $377 an ounce, a level considered critical by analysts.
A drop below $377 would likely signal significant losses towards $374 an ounce, dealers and analysts said.
"All big support lines get tested, and the feeling is it might dip below there," one dealer said.
"There are more bears about now," another noted. "This time of year you get sell-offs because the jewellery industry has done its business and business is very quiet."
Price charts showed the other precious metals also vulnerable to the downside, analysts said.
Silver was off the days lows and indicated unchanged from Monday's London close at $4.89/$4.91. But it was down eight cents from the highs of a rally late last Friday.

"On Friday silver shot up on shortcovering, which briefly stopped the selling in gold. But as soon as silver showed weakness, gold started being sold again," a dealer noted. The platinum market was quiet but prices were sinking lower along with gold and silver, dealers said.
Platinum was indicated at $383.00/$384.00 an ounce, down $1.00, while palladium was down $0.50 at $117.50/$118.50.
